title: Should You Invest in the iShares U.S. Utilities ETF (IDU)?
author: Na
description: The iShares U.S. Utilities ETF (IDU) is a passively managed fund with $1.35 billion in assets tracking the Dow Jones U.S. Utilities Index. With a 0.38% expense ratio and 2.49% dividend yield, it offers diversified exposure to the utilities sector but has underperformed year-to-date, declining 2.57%. The fund holds 49 stocks with top positions in NextEra Energy (11.1%), Southern Company, and Duke Energy. Alternatives like Vanguard Utilities ETF (VPU) and State Street Utilities SPDR (XLU) offer lower expense ratios.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The ETF offers reasonable diversification and competitive expense ratios, but has underperformed with a 2.57% year-to-date decline and a 'Hold' Zacks ETF Rank of 3. It represents a stable but not exceptional investment option.

title: IDACORP Hikes Dividend 2.3% to Strengthen Shareholder Returns
author: Na
description: IDACORP Inc. announced a 2.3% increase in its quarterly dividend to 90 cents per share ($3.60 annualized), marking its 14th consecutive year of dividend increases. The company plans to invest nearly $7 billion during 2026-2030 to strengthen generation capacity and infrastructure. IDACORP's stable regulated operations in Idaho and growing customer base support its ability to maintain consistent dividend growth.

title: BWX Technologies Already Builds Reactors for the Navy. Why Is It Still the Cheapest Nuclear Stock?
author: James Halley
description: BWX Technologies trades at lower valuations than nuclear peers despite being the sole supplier of reactors and fuel for the U.S. Navy's submarine and aircraft carrier fleets. The company reported 18% revenue growth to $901.6M in Q2, signed $1.4B in new Navy contracts, and raised full-year guidance to $3.8B revenue and $4.70-$4.80 EPS. With an $8.6B backlog and diversification into commercial nuclear and medical isotopes, BWX presents a value opportunity in the nuclear sector.

title: Should You Invest in the State Street Utilities Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLU)?

description: XLU, a passively managed utilities sector ETF launched in 1998, offers low-cost exposure to the utilities sector with a 0.08% expense ratio and $21.9 billion in assets. The fund has delivered 1.09% year-to-date returns and 3.78% over the past year, with a medium-risk profile (beta of 0.57).
